clue.text: Not finished in race crossing lake

indicators.note: the word for race straddles the lake letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to race is to compete
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A runner who has not finished, still out on a course that crosses a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unfinished is lacking parts, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Primarily Andean civilisation new imperialists overturned

definitions.text: Primarily Andean civilisation new imperialists overturned

indicators.note: in a down light, overturned means the picked letters are read from the bottom up
primarily asks for the opening letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: A history note: an Andean civilisation brought down by newly arrived imperialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' takes the heads A, C, N, I and 'overturned' turns them round; the whole clue also describes the Spanish conquest of the Inca empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire was the great Andean civilisation conquered by Spanish imperialists in the 1500s.

clue.text: Brown vehicle male wrecked

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: wrecked says the letters of male are smashed up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A brown car belonging to a man has been written off.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a light brown colour, named after the cooked sugar.

clue.text: Horse entrails around area which skiers might descend

indicators.note: the two words sit around the area letter, one each side

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding
entrails are the insides, the guts

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of a horse's guts spread over a ski slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers come down the slopes of a peak, so the description points to those slopes.

clue.text: Slimy material — maybe, Astley's verse

parts.note: lime here is birdlime, a sticky substance smeared on branches to trap birds
Rick Astley is the singer, so his first name is an example of a name, hence maybe

explanation.surface: A gibe that the singer Rick Astley's lyrics are slimy stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick Astley is the 1980s British pop singer of Never Gonna Give You Up.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is a comic five-line poem, a kind of verse.

clue.text: Mounted clip gripping fashionable garment

indicators.note: in a down light, mounted means the letters climb, reading from the bottom up
the word for clip holds the fashionable word inside it

parts.note: to clip is to cut
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A soldier's mounted uniform held by a stylish clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' gives CINUT, which 'Mounted' then reads upwards; 'Mounted' looks like it describes a cavalryman but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose or close-fitting jacket or smock, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Grew old in captivity; about to be released

indicators.note: the letter for about is let go from the word, leaving the rest

parts.note: caged means held in captivity
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A prisoner who grew old inside and is finally due for release.
explanation.definitionFit: To have grown old is to have become elderly, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Cook's good sieve

definitions.note: read as 'Cook is': to griddle is to cook on a flat iron plate

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: A kitchen item: the chef's fine sieve.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', so the definition is the verb cook.
explanation.definitionFit: To griddle food is to cook it on a hot flat iron plate.

clue.text: Upset from upside-down puddings I had

indicators.note: in a down light, upside-down means the whole string is read from the bottom up

parts.note: puddings, in British usage, are desserts
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone upset at being served upside-down puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside-down' reverses DESSERTSID to give DISTRESSED; puddings is British for sweet courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset as an adjective means anxious or troubled, a synonym.

clue.text: Island having one hundred and four bats

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters of four are scrambled

explanation.surface: An island home to a hundred and four bats.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Fellow learner and I enthralled by professor's instruments

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the learner and I are held captive inside the professor word

parts.note: a don is a university teacher; with the 's it gives DONS
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student and I captivated by an academic's collection of instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandolins are small lute-like stringed instruments, an example of the category.

clue.text: Drink before leaving stone fort hero adventurer sampled

indicators.note: sampled says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An adventurer having a quick drink in a stone fort before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A last drink taken just before departing is an idiom for the final glass.

clue.text: Misrepresented Edam: rare Dutch cheese

indicators.note: misrepresented means presented wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that Edam was wrongly sold as a rare Dutch cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A mature cheddar is a long-aged, sharp variety of hard English cheese.

clue.text: Control station and inspect part of railway

parts.note: to check is to inspect
points are the movable rails where railway tracks divide

explanation.surface: Railway staff told to inspect the track at a control station.
explanation.definitionFit: A border or security post where people are stopped and inspected is a control station.

clue.text: Appropriate measure

definitions.meaning: to appropriate is to steal; in Cockney rhyming slang ... means pinch
a length of one twenty-fourth of a foot

explanation.surface: A suitable measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang (London street slang) swaps a word for a rhyming phrase: pinch, to steal, becomes half-inch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for pinch, to steal, and also a small unit of length.

clue.text: Cases containing king's underwear

indicators.note: the word for cases holds the king letter inside it

parts.note: boxes are cases
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Suitcases packed with the king's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers, short for boxer shorts, are loose men's underpants.

clue.text: Nest made untidy with hull, covering for seed

indicators.note: made untidy says the letters of the two words are messed up together

explanation.surface: A bird's nest left messy, with a seed hull lying in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard shell around a nut kernel is a seed's protective casing.

clue.text: Artistic movement from ballet's lead absorbed in music playing

indicators.note: the picked letter is taken inside the rearranged letters
playing suggests the letters of music are performed in a new order
lead is the front letter of the word ballet's

explanation.surface: An art movement inspired by the lead ballerina dancing to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges MUSIC to CUISM, and 'absorbed in' puts B within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism was the early 20th-century art movement of Picasso and Braque.

clue.text: British PM once coming up on Queen's comms device

indicators.note: in a down light, coming up means the name reads upwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A former British prime minister getting the Queen's messaging gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper is a pager, a small radio gadget that beeps to summon its wearer.

clue.text: Bet European gondolier uses one

parts.note: to punt is to bet
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A bet on a European gondolier.
explanation.definitionFit: Boatmen who push a flat boat along with a long staff use one, so the description fits.

clue.text: Start to leave seat, an item of furniture

indicators.note: the opening letter of the seat word departs

parts.note: one's seat is one's bottom

explanation.surface: Someone getting up from a seat, which is a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to leave' removes B from BOTTOM, leaving OTTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low upholstered seat or footstool, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Young lad one treated with respect

indicators.note: treated means processed, so the letters of the words are reworked

explanation.surface: A young boy who is shown respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A preadolescent is a child not yet a teenager, so the word fits young.

clue.text: Look over island on river

indicators.note: in a down light, over places the look word on top of what follows

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
re means on or about, regarding

explanation.surface: Peering out over an island in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France.

clue.text: Bird close to leftover cut loaf

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word leftover
cut means the word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: loaf is slang for head, from rhyming slang loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A bird pecking near a leftover sliced loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is British slang for use your head, from rhyming slang loaf of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird resembling an ostrich.

clue.text: One by piano in Titanic is unmoved

indicators.note: by means next to, so the numeral sits beside what follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the piano letter goes inside the word for titanic

parts.note: titanic means massive

explanation.surface: Someone at the piano on the Titanic, calm as it sinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' looks like the ship but is the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means showing no emotion, so unmoved is a synonym.

clue.text: Enthusiasm from old pub receiving award

indicators.note: the old pub letters take the award in between them

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A lively old pub celebrating a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph means energy and zest, so it is a synonym for enthusiasm.

clue.text: Ran to lesson in school

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject

explanation.surface: A pupil who hurried to a lesson at school.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is a standard subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Tore, past tense of tear, means rushed or dashed, as ran does.

clue.text: Poison boy consumed in Lebanon, sadly

indicators.note: the boy word is swallowed within the rearranged letters
sadly means unfortunately, here signalling the letters of Lebanon are scrambled

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy poisoned in Lebanon, a sad story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' gives BELONNA, and 'consumed in' places the boy word within it, after BEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna, deadly nightshade, is a toxic plant used as a poison.
